Greatness & Goodness
Radley College is a proudly traditional boarding school, offering boys aged 13-18 an outstanding all-round education.
A Radleian is recognisable by his drive and ambition, his confidence and kindness, his loyalty and integrity, and his love of life.
Meet the Warden
Whilst society has often leaned towards a utilitarian pursuit of tangible outcomes, Radley has maintained a steadfast belief in the importance of good character. In a challenging and changing world, it is not merely skills, knowledge and expertise that will define success in the modern workplace but the ability to act with conviction, creativity and kindness.
It is our privilege to help shape the character of our boys such that they become people of real value: wherever they are and whatever they do.
Radley Schools Group
At Radley College, we are proud to be part of Radley Schools Group which brings together eight schools - Radley College, Barfield, Beeston Hall, Chandlings, Cothill, Kitebrook, Mowden Hall and West Hill Park, benefitting more than 2,300 children across the country.
Defining Radley
Our four strategic pillars shape our thinking and define our vision. Combined, they are the bedrock of a Radley education.
People
We believe in providing opportunities for a greater number of talented and deserving boys.
Place
We recognise the importance of providing world class teaching in world class facilities.
Purpose
Understanding, skills and global awareness are essential to contribute positively to a changing world.
Partnership
To enact positive change locally and nationally is an essential part of our role.
Experience Radley
Learn
We aim to nurture intellectual entrepreneurs; boys who use their strong academic understanding to solve real-world problems. Exam results matter and our excellent A-Level and GCSE results evidence our commitment to strong academic outcomes. But we know that life doesn’t have a syllabus, so we work hard to equip our boys with the skills, characteristics and values that will enable them to thrive beyond Radley.
Live
From the moment they arrive our boys are immersed in a thriving community. In their boarding house, they join a band of brothers who will have their back through thick and thin. In their year group, they bond over shared learning experiences and develop lifelong friendships. And as part of our whole school community, where they are seen, heard and known as an individual.
Apply
We offer places to boys with talent and ambition. Through our admissions process, we identify boys who will get stuck in, give their all and make the most of the endless opportunities on offer here. Our generous funding programmes allow us to bring the very best boys to Radley regardless of their ability to pay our fees, so we encourage families from all walks of life to come and see us.
Boarding Life
What could be better than living with your best mates for five years? I don't know what boarding is like at other schools, but it can't be more fun than this.
Where next?
Whether it's the excitement of sport, the buzz of lively academic debate, or the exhilaration of music and drama – there's always something happening at Radley College. Find out for yourself.

Schools across Abingdon were ringing with music this week, as thousands of children took part in the annual Music Flood Week (22–26 September).
Founded in 2021, Music Flood brings together primary and secondary schools to ensure every child has access to inspiring musical opportunities – from singing and performing in concerts, to learning an instrument, taking part in workshops, and experiencing live music from professional performers. This unique partnership is led by Radley College alongside Abingdon Music Centre, Thames Vale Youth Orchestra, Larkmead School, John Mason School, Europa School, and 16 local primaries. Its aim is simple: Music in every school, every day. During the week, over 80 pupils from Radley College, together with students from Larkmead and John Mason schools, visited 16 local primary schools – reaching thousands of children through 65 separate events, including:
The week culminated in a mass celebration event on Thursday 26 September at 10.30am in Abingdon Market Place, with more than 500 children performing alongside Music Flood’s musicians-in-residence Doikayt, a renowned klezmer ensemble, in an hour of singing, dancing and music. Doikayt, together with pupils from Radley College and Larkmead School, also busked around Abingdon, visited local primaries, and performed a public concert at Radley College on Thursday, 25 September.

At Caldecott Primary School, the number of children learning instruments has doubled, the orchestra has tripled in size, and songs learned during Music Flood “echoed through the school for weeks.”

Music Flood also continues throughout the year with the Mighty Orchestra Project, run in partnership with Radley College, Abingdon Music Centre and Thames Vale Youth Orchestra (TVYO). This brings together hundreds of young musicians, from beginners to advanced, to perform in massed orchestras. In July, 300 young musicians performed at Birmingham Symphony Hall for the National Festival of Music for Youth. This September saw the launch of the new Thames Vale Intermediate Orchestra (TVIO), offering a pathway for young musicians inspired by Mighty Orchestra workshops to join a weekly ensemble.

On Monday, the Removes were delighted to welcome Betty Abeng, the CEO of the Commonwealth Education Trust, who shared her gratitude to the boys for their fundraising efforts last term.
Head of Partnerships John Moule commented, “The funds raised will support the Trust’s work in training teachers and widening access to education for children in lower‑income countries where educational opportunity is most limited. The boys presented Betty with a cheque for £10,876 – a record amount raised by a Remove year group. I’d like to take this chance to thank parents, family, and friends for their generosity in sponsoring the various fundraising activities that took place last term. We will be sharing the impact report from the charity in the coming months as we track the impact the money has had on education throughout the Commonwealth.”

This week we are celebrating Radley’s Partnerships Week – in 2024/2025, College boys spent 4330 total hours delivering partnership support for schools and local organisations, these collaborations thriving on mutual benefit and collective commitment. Today, we highlight the story of Frank (V,C) and the lessons he as a Radley student has learned from partnerships:
“This year, I’ve been working with two students from Broadway Academy as part of the Future Ready Programme. We’ve spent time together going to lessons and sharing parts of our school days. At first, it’s a bit awkward – you’ve only just met and don’t really know what the other person’s into or what to talk about. But as you get to know each other, you find loads of shared interests.
“A real turning point for me as visiting Broadway and experiencing their school environment and daily routines. I hadn’t realised how central religion was to their day – the number of times they pray, and how on Fridays they all come together in the sports hall, which turns into a mini mosque for a short time during lunch. You learn what’s respectful to say, and that builds real understanding and empathy.
“It’s important to have these deeper conversations. For the boys involved who give their time, it’s really beneficial… having groups from both schools working together and getting to know each other is valuable. Seeing these similarities is something I’ll carry with me, not just at Radley but wherever I go.”

Our final post for Radley’s Partnerships Week tells the story of Nora Ward, Headteacher of The Oxford Academy, and how rowing partnership initiatives have built confidence and resilience amongst her students:
“Whilst for our children, rowing was an aspiration, it really began in terms of hierarchy of needs: safety for children and access to swimming, in a time when it was really difficult for our children to access these opportunities. When I said to Radley, ‘Well, actually, this is something I’m really worried about, and this is something I need help with,’ [it] came back and said, ‘We can work with you to help you solve that’. It speaks to Radley’s core purpose.
“In terms of benefits to the children, specifically thinking about the rowing programme, we joke – but we’re not really joking – about the fact that someday we’re going to have an Olympic rower among them! Of course, our young people are gaining a skill they never would have had access to if they hadn’t had the opportunity to join the rowing academy with your boys and use those facilities. Seeing themselves as rowers and accessing something they either knew nothing about before or perhaps thought, ‘This isn’t for people like me’, is truly transformative. They are overcoming obstacles and seeing themselves as successful… we all know it’s happening every time we have a conversation with those kids.
“These children were at risk of not achieving any qualifications and also being permanently excluded from school. For their parents to be able to say ‘you’re giving my child what they need’ is significant. I wouldn’t have been able to put that offer together without working in partnership with Radley.”

We continue our celebration of Radley’s Partnerships Week with Samantha Craig, a KS2 teacher from Caldecott School, and the wider impact of Music Flood – the music education initiative bringing together primary and secondary schools to ensure access to inspiring musical opportunities:
“Through Music Flood, I attended CPD sessions where I learned how to run a choir and lead singing assemblies. I picked up many tips and ideas. Even from Music Flood week, I’ve continued using them in my assemblies. Our teachers’ confidence has definitely grown… In the four years I’ve been here, I’ve seen a huge change. More children are now learning musical instruments at our school – twice as many as before.
“The orchestra days are absolutely amazing. The first year, about 10 children participated. This year, over 30 children are taking part! It’s growing each year. More children want to join. I recorded the music from the orchestra day and played it in assemblies. The children were amazed and wanted to join. It inspired them.
“For the children, Music Flood is about awe and wonder. They’re amazed by what they can do and can’t wait to tell their friends, ‘You have to go next year; it was incredible.’”

Partnerships
At the heart of our partnerships programme is a determination to enact positive change; for the remarkable organisations we work with and in our boys. We have the resource, expertise, and enthusiasm to make a difference, but we have just as much to learn as we have to give. Our growing portfolio of meaningful, sustainable and mutually beneficial collaborations with schools, charities and community groups is central to our core purpose: to inspire greatness and nurture goodness. We are proud of the work we do and are honoured to grow in tandem with outstanding, purpose-driven organisations.
Radley’s impressive partnerships scheme is making waves locally and nationally.
One of my favourite Bible quotes says, ‘act justly, love mercy and walk humbly’. This, to me, perfectly encapsulates the impact of partnership work on our boys. We want them to have good morals, understand the world around them and seek to make it better, and do so without fuss or celebration.
Thanks to our partnership with Radley College, hundreds more children and young people in Oxfordshire can now swim, ride a bike and enjoy rowing. We’re looking forward to reaching many more children in the coming years.
Academic
We champion academic excellence wherever it is found, collaborating with local schools to share opportunities and raise aspiration.
We are proud to be part of the OX14 Learning Partnership, a collaboration of local state and independent secondary schools. Together, we champion innovation in Abingdon. Through our primary STEPS programme we provide enrichment for MAGT children, and our primary reading and maths mentoring projects offer additional, targeted support.
Music
We strive for a reality where every child enjoys an inspiring music education.
Alongside our community of 25 local primary and secondary schools, we bring unique and life enhancing musical experiences to local children and equip teachers with the confidence and capability to deliver outstanding music lessons every day of the year. Our boys benefit from shared experiences and by leading on musical activities; often in collaboration with renowned professional musicians.
Respect
We are deeply committed to single sex education but recognise the benefits of targeted and meaningful collaboration.
The Respect Project, our partnership with Downe House, an independent girls’ school, fosters friendship and respect through regular academic, social and co-curricular activities. The comradeship that has developed between the two schools allows pupils to debate significant societal issues, ensuring contrasting perspectives are heard, valued and respected.
Sport
We harness the power of sport to tackle injustice and raise aspiration.
Our strategic partnership with Active Oxfordshire aims to challenge health inequalities in the most economically deprived areas of our county by providing opportunities for children and young people to live a more active life. Our Young Sports Leaders lead targeted projects in schools, with charities and at Radley in pursuit of this lofty aim.
Partnership Stories
Character
We believe contrasting contexts are a catalyst for friendship and symbiotic growth.
Shared values are the bedrock for our significant and growing partnership with Broadway Academy, a large state secondary school in Perry Barr, Birmingham. Regular and innovative academic, co-curricular and social collaboration rarely fails to highlight our similarities yet allows our boys to explore and celebrate their differences in a thoughtful way.
Countryside
We enjoy a unique rural location and use it to support local people who need a helping hand.
Our Countryside Centre is the hub for three core strands of partnership work: countryside-based alternative provision for teenagers on the cusp of exclusion from school, programmes of mental and physical health rehabilitation for charities working with the disabled and supported people, and the engagement in rural education for local primary schools. The growth of our programme for Radleians will prepare our boys to lead and assist these exciting and important projects.
International
We prepare our boys for a global world; broadening awareness of cultural differences and international development challenges.
Our developing global student exchange programme complements a partnership with the Commonwealth Education Trust, which helps to build an understanding of learning poverty and the role education plays in pursuit of growth.
Community
We play an active role in our local area, harnessing the power of community to a real difference.
Through our community partnership programme, we work alongside local charities on special projects that make Radley and the surrounding areas a better place to live and work. Boys and staff work hand-in-hand with local people, contributing to the unity between the College and our neighbours.
Where next?
Whether it's the excitement of sport, the buzz of lively academic debate, or the exhilaration of music and drama – there's always something happening at Radley College. Find out for yourself.

Pool Parties
Celebrate a special day with the very popular, exclusive pool party package for only £300. Early booking is essential. We want you to enjoy your child's party every bit as much as your child. To help you achieve this, we will set up the party tea room with tables, chairs, table cloths, plates, napkins, and bottled water. Our party tea room provides perfect viewing for the pool party so you don't have to miss any of the party whilst setting up the food. If you have any questions, please email SportsCentre@radley.org.uk
What is included? - Private use of the pool, with an inflatable obstacle course, diving boards, and an array of floats and balls, for up to 70-minutes. - Use of the party room for 50-minutes. Suitable for up to 30 children. All children must be at least 8 yrs old and able to swim 25 metres unaided and be confident in deep water. Book now directly through the website, using the link below.
FAQ's
We have booked a party but now need to change the date, is this possible?
Pool parties cannot be cancelled or refunded once booked. There may be a possibility to change your date, but this cannot be guaranteed. To enquire about changing the date, please email SportsCentre@radley.org.uk
Do you provide food?
No, we provide, tables, table cloths, plates, napkins and bottled water.
What time should I order the food for?
Children will be in the pool from 11:00/14:30 until approximately 12:10/15:40. Children then need to get changed very quickly so it is best to order food for arrival for 12:15/15:45
Do we have access to a kettle or tea and coffee making facilities?
We can put a kettle for you in the viewing gallery but there are no actual Tea or Coffee facilities available. There is a vending machine in the Sports Centre that serves a variety of Tea, Coffee and Hot Chocolate.
What is the best address to give to the children attending?
The Postcode for the Swimming Pool is OX14 2HR, please ensure that all people use the Sports Centre driveway and entrance and not the Main College entrance.
What time should I ask people to turn up?
Please ensure that everyone arrives for 10:50/14:20 to allow the children time to get changed and be on poolside by 11:00/14:30.
Will there be lifeguards?
Yes, we will have three fully qualified lifeguards on duty throughout the party.
We have a few attending who are under 8 years old, is this ok?
That is fine but any children under 8 will need to be supervised by an adult in the pool.

Training Courses
We run National Pool Lifeguard Qualification (NPLQ) during most school holidays. The National Pool Lifeguard Qualification (NPLQ) is the most widely recognised lifeguard qualification in the UK & Ireland and is a recruitment requirement for a number of jobs from Pool Lifeguard to Centre Manager. At only £200.00, this course is exceptional value for money and considerably cheaper than other local courses. Any cancellations must be made at least six weeks in advance of the booking. Please email SportsCentre@radley.org.uk to cancel.
On successful completion of the course you will be fully qualified to work as a Pool Lifeguard. All our NPLQs have the Automated External Defibrillation (AED) unit integrated into the course, so you will receive the Level 2 Automated External Defibrillation (AED) qualification if you pass the overall NPLQ assessment.
Callum (trainer) was well prepared, helpful, informative and happy to answer any questions. The friendly environment was great to train in and made me feel comfortable. The course itself was beneficial and I learnt a lot!
Information
Requirements
In accordance to the Royal Life Saving Society UK, to qualify all candidates should be able to:
Swim 50m in less than 1 minute
Swim 100m continuously
Climb out of the pool unaided
Benefits
The benefits of completing this course include:
Varied working hours
Work within a team
Level 3 qualification worth 8 UCAS points

Policies & Inspections
The Independent Schools Inspectorate visited Radley in January 2026. The inspection team found us to be meeting all standards and identified Radley’s partnership programme as a significant strength:
“Through the school’s ‘partnership programme’, pupils work in close and meaningful partnership with a wide range of schools, community groups and other organisations. Leaders regularly measure the effectiveness of the programme and actively seek pupil feedback which they consider in future planning. Through these experiences, pupils develop a broader life experience and grow in leadership skills, confidence, responsibility and social awareness.”
The report also praised the “The broad and thoughtfully designed curriculum [which] promotes intellectual curiosity and enables pupils to develop knowledge, skills and understanding across a wide range of subjects.” and the “positive culture which has at its heart the values of humility, kindness, responsibility and duty. This ensures warm, positive relationships between teachers and pupils.”
We are delighted that an experienced team of inspectors has recognised the quality of the education we offer.

Our new Music School
We are thrilled to announce the opening of our new music school!
Music At Radley
The sound of all those boys singing with such sincerity gave us rather a lump in the throat.
The refurbished Silk Hall
16 music practice rooms

Music at Radley
Singing
Our boys are fiercely proud of Radley’s singing tradition and visitors are regularly left speechless at the quality of, and passion for, singing at the College.
In Chapel, singing is led by our 120-strong Chapel Choir which comprises our boys and 25 choristers from local primary and prep schools. In recent years, they have sung Evensong at Westminster Abbey, Queen’s College Oxford and Portsmouth Cathedral, and toured France, Spain and Czech Republic. The annual Inter-Social Partsong competition is by far the most popular event in the College calendar. Directed entirely by boys, their close harmony singing is – without fail – excellent.
Ensembles
The Symphony Orchestra is our flagship instrumental ensemble. There is also a String Orchestra, Brass Ensemble, Concert Band, Big Band and Percussion Ensemble. Membership of these is by recommendation by instrumental teachers.
We have a thriving programme of smaller Chamber Ensembles at all levels, usually led by specialist Visiting Instrumental Teachers. The guitar trio and saxophone trio were finalists in this year’s Pro Corda National Chamber Music Festival. Boys can also form their own ensembles, and there are opportunities to conduct and rehearse the larger ensembles. Ensembles perform at concerts in our own concert hall, Silk Hall, as well as at prestigious venues such as the Sheldonian Theatre and Cadogan Hall.
Opening Season Concerts
The Music Department is home to boys of all musical persuasions. Those with classical interests can explore solo, chamber and orchestral repertoire to a very high standard, supported by some of the South East's leading teachers. Boys who DJ or have formed a band can record and release music on our new label, Radley Records, and give live performances at our regular bands nights. And those who are just finding their feet musically are supported and encouraged. Increasingly, I feel the department is like another Social, where boys of all year groups mix freely and explore their passions and interests together.
Music Lessons
Almost half our boys have singing or instrumental lessons.
We are proud to offer lessons in all of the orchestral instruments as well as bagpipes, drum kit, euphonium, guitar, harp, harpsichord, jazz piano, music technology, organ, percussion, saxophone, and even DJing. Our team of visiting music teachers comprises some of the finest musicians in the South East, many of whom regularly play with top orchestras or in the pit of West End shows.
Instrumental music Lessons
Solo Performance
Boys at all levels of experience have opportunities to perform as soloists, whether in weekly informal coffee concerts or high profile concerto performances alongside the College Orchestra.
The Visiting Recital Series brings some of the finest professional musicians to Radley College to lead masterclasses and workshops, with evening concerts open to all.
Bands and Recording
Our popular weekly bands night is the most-loved aspect of a popular music programme which includes band mentoring, performance opportunities, jam sessions and recordings.
This is supported by the team of guitar, singing and drum teachers, and the DJ teacher who also specialises in music production. The annual Battle of the Bands showcases many of these groups, alongside regular Live Lounge evenings and recordings for Radley Records.

In addition to our well-equipped fitness suite and weights room, we have a 25m swimming pool, squash courts and weekly workout classes. Amazing value for money! The classes are brilliantly run by great staff and is a great environment to exercise.
Leisure Club Membership
Whether you’re looking for a long-term commitment or a short pass whilst you’re in the area, you can choose a membership that’s right for you with our huge range of flexible membership options and payment plans. All members have access to our fitness suite, weights room, swimming pool and classes.
To purchase a Direct Debit Membership or a Joint Annual Membership, please visit the Sports Centre Reception. Other membership options can be purchased in person or online by clicking below.

Circuits
Our ever-popular Circuits class takes place on a Monday night. With a range of exercises, the class is suitable for guests of all abilities. Booking opens exactly two weeks before any class. Please cancel any class you cannot attend, even at late notice, as this will allow someone from the waiting list to be added to the class.
Body Burn
BodyBurn is a full-body workout, working with low weights and high reps. This class is perfect for improving muscular endurance and toning up the legs, arms and core. Booking opens exactly two weeks before any class. Please cancel any class you cannot attend, even at late notice, as this will allow someone from the waiting list to be added to the class.
F.I.T
F.I.T is a functional interval training class. Led by experienced instructors, the class is an all-body workout and uses all areas of our fitness suite. Booking opens exactly two weeks before any class. Please cancel any class you cannot attend, even at late notice, as this will allow someone from the waiting list to be added to the class. This class is not available to non-members.
Yoga
We run Vinyasa style yoga, led by our lovely instructor Sabine. Sessions take place on a Tuesday evening. Booking opens exactly two weeks before any class. Please cancel any class you cannot attend, even at late notice, as this will allow someone from the waiting list to be added to the class.
Dance Fit
A combination of dance choreography and aerobic movements provides a mood boosting cardio workout. No prior dance experience is required. Booking opens exactly two weeks before any class. Please cancel any class you cannot attend, even at late notice, as this will allow someone from the waiting list to be added to the class.
Pilates
Pilates is a series of exercises that focuses on core strength, balance, flexibility, and posture. It’s a mind-body activity that involves controlled breathing and precise movements.
Barre Balance
This class will involves a full-body workout designed to improve mobility, posture, core strength and body awareness, all through low impact movements. It’s ideal for all fitness levels with no dance experience needed! Expect a low-pressure, feel-good workout in a relaxed setting. With calming music, supportive instruction, and exercises tailored to your needs, you’ll move between the barre and mat to build strength and flexibility. Barre Balance is a combination of the control of Yoga, the alignment of Ballet and the mobility of Pilates.
Aqua FIT
Aqua FIT is a low-impact, full-body workout that combines cardio, strength training, and flexibility exercises in a pool
